one_line_description.value: Brex is a unified spend platform offering global corporate cards, expense management, reimbursements, travel, and bill pay.
one_line_description.quote: Brex is the first fully unified spend platform — with global corporate cards, expense management, reimbursements, travel, and bill pay.

has_public_api.quote: Using the Brex API, you can power your internal tools and create custom workflows.

api_type.quote: Brex APIs use the REST architecture, are defined using the OpenAPI specification and use standard HTTP response codes and verbs.

api_breadth.value: REST/OpenAPI, 10 documented API groups (Accounting, Budgets, Expenses, Fields, Onboarding, Payments, Team, Transactions, Travel, Webhooks), read-write (e.g. 'manage users, locations, departments, and cards')
api_breadth.quote: - Accounting API: View and manage accounting data - Budgets API: Manage budgets and budget programs - Expenses API: View and manage card expenses data, receipt match and receipt uploads

docs_url.quote: Explore our guides and review our API documentation to see how you can integrate with Brex.

auth_methods.quote: For clients that don't support OAuth, or for programmatic access, account and card admins can authenticate with a Brex API token.

oauth_scopes_documented.quote: Scopes define which endpoints your app has access to. You will specify your scopes when generating your user token.

access_model.quote: Real-time reporting - Brex API access - Bill pay - Reimbursements

access_notes.value: Requires an existing Brex customer account; only an account admin or card admin can generate a user token (Settings > Developer) after the company accepts the Developer API agreement. Brex currently exposes only a production API server at https://api.brex.com — no sandbox. The pricing page lists 'Brex API access' as a plan feature, and no free/self-serve developer edition is documented; partner/onboarding API uses client credentials and is reserved for Brex developer partners.
access_notes.quote: If your company has not accepted the developer API agreement, please review the terms and conditions. These must be accepted to use the developer API.

official_mcp_server.quote: The server is hosted at `https://api.brex.com/mcp` and supports any MCP-compatible client.

rate_limits.value: Per Client ID and Brex account: 1,000 requests per 60 seconds; 1,000 transfers per 24 hours; 100 international wires per 24 hours; 5,000 cards created per 24 hours; HTTP 429 when exceeded
rate_limits.quote: - Up to 1,000 requests in 60 seconds. - Up to 1,000 transfers in 24 hours. - Up to 100 international wires in 24 hours. - Up to 5,000 cards created in 24 hours.

webhooks.quote: Webhooks API: Send real-time notifications based on events

sandbox_or_test_env.quote: Brex currently only offers a production API server at `https://api.brex.com`. This is the base URL for all API calls.

api_versioning_or_deprecation_notes.value: No formal versioning/sunset policy captured; changelog states updates are rolling and unscheduled, and the changelog shows endpoints being removed as deprecated (e.g. POST /v2/users/{id}/limit). API paths are versioned (/v2).
api_versioning_or_deprecation_notes.quote: This changelog tracks changes to the Brex API and is updated periodically. Updates to the API are on a rolling basis and not on any defined schedule.

verdict_reason: Brex has a genuinely broad, well-documented REST/OpenAPI surface (ten API groups, documented OAuth scopes, rate limits, webhooks) and even a vendor-hosted MCP server at https://api.brex.com/mcp. However, credentials are not generally self-serve: the quickstart 'assumes you are a Brex customer with admin access' and the auth guide requires account/card-admin token creation plus acceptance of the Developer API agreement. API access is listed only as a plan feature and the sole server is production, so access is gated rather than trivially self-serve.
main_blocker: Requires an existing Brex customer account with account/card-admin role; production-only, no sandbox
open_questions: Is a Brex account obtainable self-serve and free, or does it require sales contact? The bundle shows 'Brex API access' as a plan feature but no prices, free-tier terms, or signup flow.
Which Brex plan tiers include API access? The pricing page feature list does not unambiguously map features to tier columns.
Does Brex ship any official, vendor-maintained SDKs? No source in the bundle confirms this (a community-supported libraries page appeared only as a search snippet, not in the fetched sources).

Partner/onboarding API access (client-credentials grant, partner authentication) appears restricted to Brex developer partners, but the partner onboarding/application requirements were not fully captured in the evidence.
The team API snippet mentions a staging server that 'is not a sandbox' but that page was not included in the SOURCES text, so it was not used.
